name: Kemi Saami
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct (~1900s); only MED is Schefferus 1673 Lapponia (ethnography, not a phonological description); no grammar/phonology of Kemi Saami exists.

sources.citation: Kallio, Kati, Valtonen, Taarna & Jouste, Marko 2019. Olaus Sirman runojen vertailevaa luentaa – runojen poetiikka suhteessa suullisiin ja kirjallisiin lähikulttuureihin. SUSA/JSFOu 97: 109–152. doi:10.33340/susa.75266
sources.note: Metrical/poetic analysis of Sirma's two Kemi Saami poems. p. 123 (sec. 3.2): 'Selkeää säännöllistä painollisten ja painottomien tavujen vaihtelua ei runossa näytä olevan' (no clear regular alternation of stressed and unstressed syllables in the poem); p. 126 similar. Where word stress falls is not stated (implicitly the Saami/Finnic initial-stress assumption).

sources.citation: Äimä, Frans & Itkonen, Toivo 1918. Jacob Fellmanin muistiinpanot Sompion ja Kuolajärven lapinmurteista. Suomalais-Ugrilaisen Seuran Aikakauskirja / JSFOu XXX,30: 1–91 (pp. 1–33 word list ed. T. Itkonen & F. Äimä; pp. 34–91 = XXX,30a, F. Äimä, 'Äänneopillinen katsaus Sompion ja Kuolajärven lapinmurteisiin'). Helsinki: Suomalais-Ugrilainen Seura.
sources.note: The only phonological treatment of Kemi Saami (historical phonology of Fellman's 1820s written word lists). No statement of where stress falls; stress was never recorded. Äimä uses the Lappological structural terms pääpainollinen tavu (main-stressed = 1st syllable), pääpainoton, sivupainollinen (secondary-stressed) and painoton tavu as positions, e.g. §24 p. 84 'Pääpainollisen tavun vokaalit... joissa se käsittää 1. tavun koko vokaalisysteemin', §35 p. ~70 'k ~ γ vaihtelun on oletettava esiintyneen kantalapissa sivupainollisen tavun vokaalin jäljessä', and p. 60 explains a Kuolajärvi v-loss a…

sources.citation: Wiklund, K. B. 1913. En kemilapsk text från år 1716. Le Monde Oriental 7: 82–96.
sources.note: Edition of Olaus Sirma's 1716 catechism translation with philological commentary; no remark on accent or stress (no occurrences of accent/betoning/tonvikt).

sources.citation: Valtonen, Taarna 2024. Miksi keminsaame kuoli? Sosiolingvistinen rekonstruktio keminsaamen sammumiseen johtaneista tekijöistä. SUSA/JSFOu 100: 207–239. doi:10.33340/susa.140998
sources.note: Sociolinguistic history of the extinction; p. 213 summarises dialect classification (Sammallahti 1998: 26; Äimä & Itkonen 1918: 89–91). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kovář, Michal 2019. Sami texts from Kemi Sápmi recorded by Jenny and Samuli Paulaharju. AUC Philologica 2019(3): 39–44. doi:10.14712/24646830.2019.28
sources.note: Survey of the Kemi Saami corpus (Sirma 1673, catechism 1716, Fellman, Sjögren, Paulaharju fragments); fn. 6: 'we don't know, what the actual pronunciation was'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kert, G. M. 1993. Saamskij jazyk. In: Jazyki mira: Ural'skie jazyki, 134–148. Moskva: Nauka.

sources.citation: Sjögren, And. Joh. 1828. Anteckningar om församlingarne i Kemi-Lappmark. Helsingfors. (Sompio Lord's Prayer pp. 253–254, linguistic notes pp. 391–405.)
sources.note: Gives the Sompio-dialect Lord's Prayer with comparative grammatical notes; remarks on Finnish influence on pronunciation (p. 252) but nothing on accent/stress placement.

sources.citation: Valtonen, Taarna 2026. Olaus Mattsson Sirma as a Source for the Saami Culture and Language of Kemi Lappmark in Schefferus's Lapponia. In: Learned Discourses on the Indigenous in Fennoscandia and Beyond, c. 1500–1800, pp. 249–291. Leiden: Brill.

sources.note: Newest linguistic treatment of Sirma's Kemi Saami texts by the leading specialist; may discuss Sirma's orthography (acute accents) and what can and cannot be inferred about pronunciation; would supersede Kovář 2019 as the corpus overview.

sources.citation: Sammallahti, Pekka 1998. The Saami Languages: An Introduction. Kárášjohka: Davvi Girji.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: library print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan): WID WID-LC PH706.S26 1998
sources.note: Standard handbook; contains the family-wide prosody statement (initial main stress, alternating secondary stress) and the classification of the Kemi Saami varieties (p. 26). The only kind of source from which a stress value for extinct Kemi Saami could be assigned (by inheritance, second-hand).

sources.citation: Korhonen, Mikko 1981. Johdatus lapin kielen historiaan. (SKST 370.) Helsinki: Suomalaisen Kirjallisuuden Seura.

sources.note: Historical handbook of Saami with explicit sections on Proto-Saami word stress and on the extinct Kemi Saami sources; likely the most explicit statement that the inherited initial-stress system is assumed for all Saami including Kemi.

sources.note: Monograph on the extinct Kemi Lapp culture; assembles the textual remnants; cited by every later work. Not a phonology, but the fullest inventory of primary material.
